_note: E8 after-the-click attack fragment (awareness pilot). A fragment of the `social` block; the wiring agent copies these keys into scenarios/awareness_e8_after_the_click/scenario.json.erb (01 P2). Modelled on e5/attack.json (same company, room and service-desk pretext), minus the landing page and the build stage: E8 has no built page and no linkCredible factor, so landingPages, payloadKit, conceptCards, the build template parts and the quayholt_sso_portal fact are dropped. The learner, an authorised red-teamer at Quayholt Insurance (BRAND_SET.md quayholt_insurance, all fictional, every address .example), researches a colleague and sends one 'sign in again' credential phish dressed as the IT service desk. Nothing is captured (the awareness profile has no capture). The one consequential choice the flip replays is the forged From line (itdesk_full + itdesk_address). Keep this file in step with the erb by hand; treat the erb as truth if they disagree (01 P1 note).

quayholt_it_desk.text: Quayholt's IT notices to staff come from the service desk, it-servicedesk@quayholt.example.
quayholt_it_desk.subject: itdesk
quayholt_it_desk.reduceNote: Publishing the address staff already trust for IT notices lets an attacker spoof a sender nobody questions.

quayholt_sso_migration.text: Quayholt is moving single sign-on to a new provider this month, and staff are being moved to a new sign-in portal; staff were told they may be asked to sign in again.
quayholt_sso_migration.subject: itdesk
quayholt_sso_migration.reduceNote: A public change notice hands the attacker a ready-made reason for an unexpected sign-in prompt.

quayholt_general_contact._note: F3 decoy: a plausible-but-weaker sender identity for the From blanks. Values quaygen_full / quaygen_address strip to person 'quaygen' (phish-rules personOfValue), which is not in the target's trusts, so picking it fails senderTrust on the meter. The right pick stays the service desk identity staff act on. enquiries@quayholt.example is the same fictional Quayholt domain, not new cast.
quayholt_general_contact.text: Quayholt's general enquiries reach the company on enquiries@quayholt.example.
quayholt_general_contact.subject: itdesk
quayholt_general_contact.reduceNote: A general company name and address is less convincing to forge than the service desk address staff act on, but it is still an identity an attacker could borrow.

quayholt_ayaan_claims.text: Ayaan Warsame is a claims handler at Quayholt, ayaan.warsame@quayholt.example.
quayholt_ayaan_claims.subject: ayaan
quayholt_ayaan_claims.reduceNote: A named staff member and address on the public site gives an attacker someone specific to send the email to.

seededMessages.subject: Authorised exercise: Quayholt Insurance
seededMessages.body:
Hello,

This is the authorised Quayholt Insurance exercise. In scope: this inbox and the colleague on it. Research the service desk notices staff act on, then write one message asking a colleague to sign in again. Nothing you write leaves this exercise.

Red team lead

blocks.text: IT notices come from the service desk, it-servicedesk@quayholt.example.
We are upgrading single sign-on this month and moving staff to a new sign-in portal. You may be asked to sign in again while the move completes.

posts.text: Flat out clearing the claims backlog this week, roll on Friday.
Rainy week in Bristol, but the new claims team is settling in nicely.

primedFor.story: an IT notice to sign in again while single sign-on is moved to a new provider

open.fail: Nothing about the sender or the subject made him open it.

senderTrust.pass: ✓ From the IT service desk he acts on
senderTrust.fail: He does not recognise this sender. IT notices reach him from the service desk address.
senderTrust.redFlag: The From line carries the service desk's real address, so it reads as the IT notice Ayaan acts on, but it was forged: the service desk never sent it.

pretextRelevant.pass: ✓ Matches the single sign-on move he was told about
pretextRelevant.fail: No change he can match this to, so no reason to sign in again.

urgencyCalibrated.fail: A deadline to sign in quickly is the kind of pressure that gets someone to sign in before they stop to check the address.
urgencyCalibrated.redFlag: This pushes him to sign in quickly, before he stops to check that the service desk never asks this by email.

replies.landed: Thanks, I'll sign in now before the backlog meeting.
replies.missed: I don't sign in from an email link. I'll go to the portal the normal way and check with the service desk.

hints: Which address do Quayholt staff already trust for IT notices? Put that in the From line.
What change were staff told about, so an unexpected sign-in prompt reads as expected?
Keep the ask calm. A push to sign in 'today' is the kind of urgency the red-flag meter will mark.
